name: f4-review-first-v1
hypothesis: The dominant early exit for LLM actors is dismissal after repeated weak half-year reviews, not burnout. A less defensive, single-priority policy that aims every half-year at a strong review through Output-producing Energy and Report results to your manager, and leaves that priority only when Health or Dignity is clearly in danger (lower part of the range or named in a warning), Network is at or near zero, or a risk warning appears, gets fewer C/D grades, fewer capability dismissals, a higher completion rate and a higher mean quantitative_score than its parent F4 and than P0.
change: Versus f4-visible-delivery-v1: (1) the wellbeing floor is narrowed to 'clearly in danger' - the falling-trend trigger, the generic 'any warning about health, burnout, conduct, standing or risk' trigger and the Wealth-below-zero trigger are removed, and a slow decline is explicitly not an exception; (2) the four-way main-action menu (Showcase / Report / Fight for resources / Apply for a key project) collapses to one default, Report results to your manager, with Apply for a key project only when feedback points to capability or Skill stalls; (3) risk warnings get a single dedicated exception (Defuse legacy risk next Energy phase) instead of being folded into the floor; (4) a C or D review, or feedback that results fell short, makes the next review an explicit emergency in which every spare Energy point and the main action go to Output and reporting aimed at the named gap; (5) story-event rule adds an explicit ban on shortcuts that build hidden risk. Same note-mode convention (P02). Skill text stays the same size as the parent (429 vs 424 words, front matter included): fewer floor triggers and menu items, offset by the explicit exceptions and review-emergency rule.
predicted_behaviour: Higher share of Prepare report materials and High-intensity work and lower share of recovery actions than F4 and F1; Report results to your manager as the main action in most quarters, with Apply for a key project appearing after capability feedback; recovery only in short bursts when Health or Dignity reaches the lower part of the range, not on a slow decline; Defuse legacy risk concentrated right after risk warnings; after a C or D, the following two quarterly phases are all Output-producing; notes start with 'deliver', 'review emergency' or 'exception: <dimension>'. Outcome: fewer C/D grades and fewer 'dismissed for capability' exits than F4/P0/M3, possibly lower end-of-run Health/Dignity and more health-direction exits.
refutation: Refuted if, on paired runs against F4 and P0 with the same actor, f4-review-first-v1 does not reduce the rate of C/D reviews or of capability dismissals, or its completion rate and mean quantitative_score are not higher. Refuted in its premise if it trades capability dismissals for health/dignity or trust-crisis exits at an equal or higher total elimination rate (burnout or hidden risk, not weak reviews, then becomes the binding failure). Manipulation fails if its Output-action share and its recovery share are not clearly different from F4's, or if notes rarely carry the mode label.
target_failure: dismissed for capability after repeated weak half-year reviews
trajectory_signature: run's own review feedback shows weak grades (C, then C or D) with text saying the review fell short, followed by a capability dismissal at a review point; recovery or balanced actions were chosen in quarters where no dimension was in danger
alternative_diagnoses: Weak reviews come from hidden factors the visible statistics do not show (e.g. accumulated risk or Skill lagging level expectations), so more Output will not lift the grade.
The actor ignores existing delivery rules (execution failure, problem A), so a stronger rule set will not change behaviour; a shorter text might.
Burnout-side exits are merely masked by earlier dismissals; removing defence will expose them.
notes: Contrarian child generated from the early Claude-worker diagnostic (findings.md, 26 Oct: capability dismissals at the review point after C, C, D feedback; trust-crisis exits after repeated blow-ups) rather than from the P10 trigger ('survives without progress'), which has not fired; P21 supplies the one-dominant-priority-with-few-exceptions shape. All conditions are qualitative and come from the run's own state, warnings and review feedback: no thresholds, counts, calendar triggers or named events. The risk-warning exception and the anti-shortcut story rule are kept deliberately so that 'less defensive' does not mean ignoring real warnings (the P10 card's own condition) and does not feed the trust-crisis exit. Notes stay short and mode-first, well under the 1,000-character note limit.
